notes:
I don't have any notes on Jeremiah 34 for you yet, because I couldn't read any source pages.

My first attempt to fetch the pages failed because of a bug in my own code: it didn't process the reply from the fetch tool correctly. When I tried again, the tool said I had used up my calls for this turn. So I haven't read Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, NET Bible or Precept Austin, or any other site on your list.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, and I haven't read any. So I haven't written notes from memory or attached web addresses I haven't checked. That would risk claiming a source says something it doesn't.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Jeremiah 34; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com (studylight.org as a backup); Precept Austin's Jeremiah 34 page.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** pages on releasing slaves and on Zedekiah's prophesied peaceful death (vv. 4–5) from ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, gty.org, desiringgod.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), seedbed.com, lcms.org and 1517.org.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes, especially the ones on the "freedom" wordplay in v. 17 and the cut calf in vv. 18–19. Also bibleodyssey.org on ancient covenant-making rituals, and newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org if they discuss this chapter. I'll include popular modern teaching like prosperity or word-of-faith only if the allowed sites actually discuss it in connection with this chapter.

The notes will follow your format ("v. 4: …"), with a web address after each point, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
